scope_boundaries: The explicit Jacobian is a representative of the B isogeny class, not an asserted unique curve.
The Weil-restriction principal polarization is a polarization on a representative in the P46,7 isogeny class; it does not change the natural Prym polarization type (1,1,1,2).
No analytic Sato-Tate equidistribution claim is made.
No characteristic-zero decomposition of P46 is inferred from the p=7 reduction.
